events.name: Battle of Fulford
events.summary: Harald Hardrada and Tostig defeated the northern English earls near York. The point is an approximate battlefield anchor, not a reconstructed battle frontage.

events.name: Battle of Stamford Bridge
events.summary: Harold Godwinson defeated Harald Hardrada’s invading army. The battlefield’s precise extent and dispositions are debated; this is a vicinity marker.

events.name: William lands at Pevensey
events.summary: William’s invasion fleet reached the Sussex coast. The present coastline differs from that of 1066; this anchor identifies the Pevensey vicinity.

events.name: Battle of Hastings
events.summary: William defeated Harold’s army near the site now called Battle. This event did not by itself establish immediate, uniform Norman control throughout England.

events.name: Romulus Augustulus deposed
events.summary: Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus and established rule in Italy. This conventional endpoint for the western imperial office is not the simultaneous disappearance of Roman institutions or a takeover of every former western province.

campaigns.name: Harald & Tostig · Yorkshire campaign
campaigns.summary: The dated sequence starts at the Ouse anchorage and follows the two recorded battles. It does not reconstruct the voyage from Norway or the precise path between sites.

campaigns.name: William · landing and Hastings campaign
campaigns.outcome: Victory at Hastings; subsequent conquest continued
campaigns.summary: Dated landing, camp and battle anchors show the Sussex phase. The connecting arrow is illustrative and does not assert a surveyed road or constant marching speed.

relations.origin: Western imperial office of Romulus Augustulus
relations.summary: The relation concerns the imperial office and Italy. It does not turn Odoacer into the successor to all former western Roman territory. The short connector is a diagram at Ravenna, not a military route.
Hastings enabled William’s claim to the English crown. Conquest, resistance and consolidation continued after 1066. This relation is cited directly rather than inferred from adjacent polity polygons.
